title: Capacity-first Q3 Roadmap: Demand-hedging for Hosted API & Model Onboarding
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background:
As usage of the Hosted API accelerates, we need a capacity-first quarterly roadmap that ties model onboarding cadence to predictable capacity and clear hedges. Past quarters showed uneven demand spikes from partner integrations that caused degraded latencies for high-SLA customers during model rotations. This ticket defines a scenario-driven phasing plan that prioritizes availability and cost predictability when adding new models to the catalog and expanding hosted endpoints.

Objectives:
- Guarantee 99.9% p95 latency SLA for P1 customers during onboarding and rotation windows.
- Define a model onboarding runway that explicitly maps capacity commits to model weight and traffic expectations.
- Create gating criteria and rollout playbooks (canary tolerances, automatic fallback) to avoid noisy neighbor failures.
- Align OKRs: reduce production latency incidents by 40% during rollout windows; reduce unexpected capacity overrun costs by 30%.

Success metrics (what we will measure):
- Rolling p95 latency pre/post onboarding windows (target <= SLA + 10%).
- Number of rollbacks triggered by capacity infra alarms (target 0–1 per quarter).
- Percent of new hosted models with pre-approved capacity and automated fallback (target 100%).
- Cost variance vs. forecast during model additions (target < 15% deviation).

Scenarios (used to create the runway):
- Base: steady traffic growth (5–10% week-over-week). Models onboarded at standard weight (<=5% of traffic).
- Surge: partner-driven spike (+60% sustained for 48 hours). Models onboarded must be backfilled via lower-cost variants or throttled canaries.
- Long tail: many small model additions (10–15) across the quarter requiring aggregated capacity headroom.

Phasing proposal (three lanes):
- Green lane (low risk): pre-validated models, capacity pre-allocated from reserved pool, scheduled during low-traffic windows.
- Amber lane (moderate risk): models that require limited autoscaling bursts and one canary stage with automated rollback.
- Red lane (high risk): experimental or large-footprint models requiring dedicated capacity reservation and coordination with infra/ops for SLA hedging.

Gating criteria (must pass to move to next lane):
- Performance: model profile demonstrates latency and GPU memory behavior under synthetic load matching 120% of expected traffic.
- Cost: estimated incremental token cost and instance-hours approved by finance.
- Observability: tracing, end-to-end synthetic checks, and alerting configured.
- Safety & compliance: data handling review completed for private/regulated customers.

Operational playbook (short):
- Pre-launch: capacity reservation + canary route defined + run synthetic for 24h.
- Launch window: staged traffic ramp (0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100%) with p95 and error-rate checks at each step.
- Fallback: immediate switch to fallback model variant and autoscale down dangerous kernels if thresholds breached.
- Postmortem: 72h incident review for any deviation from runbook.

Stakeholders & roles:
- PM lead: Sofia Martinez (roadmap decisions, OKR linkage)
- Infra/Eng: Liam Chen (capacity planning, autoscaling playbooks), Infra SIG (kernel scheduling)
- Analytics: Maya Patel (demand forecasting, cost modeling)
- Solutions: Aisha Kapoor (customer communication & sandbox coordination)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Over-commitment of reserved capacity increases cost. Mitigation: tiered reservation + burstable pool + early canary throttles.
- Risk: Latency regressions from kernel mismatches. Mitigation: preflight kernel selection and a short warm-up traffic ramp.
- Risk: Stakeholder misalignment on release dates. Mitigation: weekly cadence sync and embedded acceptance checklist.

Deliverables (this ticket):
- Definitive Q3 runway doc with three lanes and capacity map (this ticket).
- Canary runbook template and automated rollback playbook.
- Dashboard: capacity headroom + forecast + live canary health.
- OKR mapping and monitoring dashboard queries.

Acceptance criteria:
- Execs and infra sign-off on runway and capacity hedges.
- Canary runbook validated in staging with synthetic traffic.
- Dashboard surfacing forecast vs. committed capacity and canary health.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Analytics: run demand forecast + cost sensitivity (Maya) — due 2026-01-22.
- Infra: propose reserved + burst configuration and autoscale policy (Liam) — due 2026-01-26.
- PM: finalize lane definitions and gating criteria; schedule stakeholder review (Sofia) — due 2026-01-20.
- Solutions: gather partner onboarding windows and constraints (Aisha) — due 2026-01-25.
